profile.reading: This is Polcoms Alwernia data center, located between Krakow and Katowice in southern Poland, put into service in 2015. Polcom, a Polish IT infrastructure and cloud computing company, describes the facility as spanning about 6,500 square meters with 8 megawatts of power capacity and the ability to supply up to 15 kilowatts per rack. The operator emphasizes redundancy at the site, citing dual power connections, independent cooling sources, and connectivity through twelve different telecommunications carriers for network resilience. Alwernia forms one half of Polcoms two site Krakow area data center network, paired with an earlier, larger facility at Skawina put into service in 2011, allowing the company to offer redundant colocation, cloud computing, and IT integration services with georedundancy across both sites for enterprise and public sector clients in southern Poland. Polcom describes itself as having more than 30 years in the market, with its first data center completed in 2006 before Skawina and Alwernia followed as its second and later locations; the company is headquartered at ul. Krakowska 43 in Skawina. The company reports over 300 business customers, about 70 percent with international reach across four continents, spanning finance, healthcare, retail, manufacturing, e-commerce, and public sector clients, supported by a staff of about 170 specialists, and holds Polands Polska Chmura, or Polish Cloud, certification alongside compliance with the European Cloud Sovereignty Framework. Combined, the Skawina and Alwernia sites total more than 12,000 square meters across roughly 6 hectares of secured, fenced plots, linked by independent fiber optic cable over the 24 kilometers separating them. The Alwernia facility cost about 63 million Polish zloty to build and uses direct liquid cooling technology that Polcom engineers paired with a proprietary heat recovery system for pipeline fluids, achieving a power usage effectiveness below 1.2 and cutting water heating energy consumption by about 10 percent, monitored throughout by a custom building management system.
